# Poisson equations and ODE tracking {#sec-poisson-feedback}

The augmented kernel has an invariant law $\nu_\theta$ and is geometrically contractive in Wasserstein distance under @thm-wasserstein-lifting. We use its Poisson equation to compare the adaptive recursion with the stationary mean field $F(\theta)$.

## Frozen Poisson equation

For a scalar Lipschitz observable $G_\theta$ on $\mathsf Z$, let

$$
F(\theta)=\nu_\theta(G_\theta),\qquad
\bar G_\theta=G_\theta-F(\theta).
$$ {#eq-centred-adam-observable}

The vector-valued case is understood coordinatewise. The Poisson equation is

$$
u_\theta-Q_\theta u_\theta=\bar G_\theta.
$$ {#eq-augmented-poisson}

Geometric Wasserstein contraction and finite first eccentricity give the centred Neumann solution [@Hofstadler2026, Theorem 3.4]

$$
u_\theta(z)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty
\bigl[Q_\theta^nG_\theta(z)-F(\theta)\bigr],
$$ {#eq-poisson-series}

with $\nu_\theta(u_\theta)=0$ and

$$
\|u_\theta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}(d_Z)}
\leq\Lambda_\theta\|G_\theta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}(d_Z)},
\qquad
\Lambda_\theta:=\sum_{n=0}^\infty\tau_{d_Z}(Q_\theta^n)
\leq\frac{C_Z(\eta)}{1-\eta}.
$$ {#eq-poisson-lipschitz-bound}

The square-root memory coordinates in @eq-sqrt-memory-update give a Lipschitz Adam readout for bounded innovations.

### Eccentricity and weighted growth

Let $\|h\|_{\mathcal V}=\sup_z |h(z)|/\mathcal V(z)$ and $E_{1,\theta}(z)=\int d_Z(z,z')\,\nu_\theta(dz')$. Suppose $E_{1,\theta}(z)\leq C_E\mathcal V(z)$ uniformly for $\theta\in\mathsf K$. Centring a Lipschitz function under $\nu_\theta$ gives

$$
\|f-\nu_\theta(f)\|_{\mathcal V}
\leq C_E\|f\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}.
$$ {#eq-eccentricity-weighted-embedding}

The comparison follows from the triangle inequality if $d_Z(z,z_0)\leq c\mathcal V(z)$ and $\sup_{\theta\in\mathsf K}\nu_\theta(\mathcal V)<\infty$. Applying the Neumann-series bound yields

$$
\|u_\theta\|_{\mathcal V}
\leq C_E\Lambda_\theta\|G_\theta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}.
$$ {#eq-poisson-weighted-growth}

For a zero-mass signed measure $\xi$ with finite weighted variation, duality also gives

$$
\|\xi\|_{\mathrm{KR}}
\leq C_E\int\mathcal V(z)\,|\xi|(dz).
$$ {#eq-weighted-to-wasserstein}

Eccentricity thus links the Lipschitz estimates obtained from Wasserstein contraction to the weighted-growth estimates used in [@Care2026].

## Parameter regularity of the Poisson solution

The weighted one-step perturbation bound of @prp-augmented-kernel-regularity combines with the decay of centred iterates to give a parameter modulus for the Poisson solution. This follows the comparison-of-iterates approach of [@Care2026, Theorem 2], using Wasserstein contraction on the augmented space.

::: {#prp-poisson-parameter}
## Log-Lipschitz parameter regularity

Let $\mathsf K$ be a compact parameter set. Assume uniformly over $\theta,\vartheta\in\mathsf K$ that:

1. $Q_\theta$ satisfies @eq-augmented-contraction with common constants $C_Z<\infty$ and $\rho\in(0,1)$, and has invariant law $\nu_\theta$.
2. The one-step weighted estimate @eq-weighted-pointwise-operator-bound holds, and $Q_\theta\mathcal V\leq a\mathcal V+b$ for some $a<1$, $b<\infty$.
3. $\sup_{\theta\in\mathsf K}\nu_\theta(\mathcal V)<\infty$ and $d_Z(z,z_0)\leq c\mathcal V(z)$ for some $z_0$.
4. $\sup_{\theta\in\mathsf K}\|G_\theta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}\leq L_G$ and
   $|G_\theta(z)-G_\vartheta(z)|\leq L_{G,\theta}\|\theta-\vartheta\|\mathcal V(z)$.

Assume the kernels and observables are jointly measurable in parameter and state. For $t>0$, set $\omega(t)=t(1+\log^+(1/t))$ and $\omega(0)=0$. Then there is $C<\infty$ such that

$$
|u_\theta(z)-u_\vartheta(z)|
\leq C\mathcal V(z)\omega(\|\theta-\vartheta\|).
$$ {#eq-poisson-parameter-log-lipschitz}

The same estimate holds for $\phi_\theta=Q_\theta u_\theta$:

$$
|\phi_\theta(z)-\phi_\vartheta(z)|
\leq C\mathcal V(z)\omega(\|\theta-\vartheta\|).
$$ {#eq-poisson-feedback-log-lipschitz}
:::

::: {.proof}
Put $\delta=\|\theta-\vartheta\|$ and write

$$
R_\theta^nG_\theta(z)=Q_\theta^nG_\theta(z)-F(\theta),
\qquad
D_n(z)=R_\theta^nG_\theta(z)-R_\vartheta^nG_\vartheta(z).
$$

The drift assumption gives $\sup_{\theta,n}Q_\theta^n\mathcal V(z)\leq C_V\mathcal V(z)$. By the eccentricity comparison and @eq-invariant-wasserstein-rate,

$$
|R_\theta^nG_\theta(z)|
\leq C_Z\rho^n L_GE_{1,\theta}(z)
\leq C_1\rho^n\mathcal V(z),
$$

so $|D_n(z)|\leq 2C_1\rho^n\mathcal V(z)$.

For a second bound, decompose

$$
\begin{aligned}
D_n={}&(Q_\theta^n-Q_\vartheta^n)G_\theta\\
&+Q_\vartheta^n(G_\theta-G_\vartheta)
-\bigl(F(\theta)-F(\vartheta)\bigr).
\end{aligned}
$$

The last term is $O(\delta)$ by @eq-field-parameter-bound and @cor-invariant-parameter. The middle term is at most $L_{G,\theta}C_V\delta\mathcal V(z)$. For the first term, telescope as in @eq-perturbation-telescope. Wasserstein contraction gives

$$
\|Q_\theta^kG_\theta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}
\leq C_Z\rho^kL_G.
$$

Applying @eq-weighted-pointwise-operator-bound inside the telescoping sum,

$$
\begin{aligned}
&|(Q_\theta^n-Q_\vartheta^n)G_\theta(z)|\\
&\quad\leq C_ZL_QL_G\delta
\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\rho^{n-1-j}Q_\vartheta^j\mathcal V(z)\\
&\quad\leq \frac{C_ZL_QL_GC_V}{1-\rho}\,
\delta\mathcal V(z).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-centred-iterate-parameter-bound}

Thus $|D_n(z)|\leq C_2\delta\mathcal V(z)$, uniformly in $n$. Combining the two estimates and summing the Neumann series yields

$$
\begin{aligned}
|u_\theta(z)-u_\vartheta(z)|
&\leq C_3\mathcal V(z)
\sum_{n=0}^\infty\min\{\delta,\rho^n\}\\
&\leq C_4\mathcal V(z)\omega(\delta).
\end{aligned}
$$

The logarithmic factor comes from splitting the sum at $n$ of order $\log(1/\delta)/|\log\rho|$. Finally, the Poisson identity gives $\phi_\theta=u_\theta-G_\theta+F(\theta)$. The parameter estimates for its three terms prove @eq-poisson-feedback-log-lipschitz.
:::

The parameter modulus follows from the weighted kernel perturbation already established in Section 5. Its logarithmic term measures the number of iterations required for geometric forgetting to reach the scale of a parameter change.

## Martingale decomposition and ODE tracking

Consider the adaptive recursion

$$
Z_{n+1}\mid\mathcal F_n\sim Q_{\theta_n}(Z_n,\cdot),
\qquad
\theta_{n+1}=\theta_n+\gamma_{n+1}G_{\theta_n}(Z_{n+1}).
$$ {#eq-augmented-controlled-sa}

Define

$$
\Delta M_{n+1}
=u_{\theta_n}(Z_{n+1})-Q_{\theta_n}u_{\theta_n}(Z_n),
\qquad \phi_\theta=Q_\theta u_\theta.
$$ {#eq-poisson-martingale-increment}

The Poisson equation gives

$$
G_{\theta_n}(Z_{n+1})-F(\theta_n)
=\Delta M_{n+1}
+\phi_{\theta_n}(Z_n)-\phi_{\theta_n}(Z_{n+1}).
$$ {#eq-controlled-poisson-decomposition}

The conditional mean of $\Delta M_{n+1}$ is zero. For scalar observables, its conditional variance satisfies

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\mathbb E[(\Delta M_{n+1})^2\mid\mathcal F_n]\\
&\qquad=Q_{\theta_n}u_{\theta_n}^2(Z_n)
-\bigl(Q_{\theta_n}u_{\theta_n}(Z_n)\bigr)^2.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-poisson-conditional-variance}

This is the martingale calculation in [@Laitinen2024_G3FDZQA8, Lemma 4], applied here to $Q_\theta$ on the augmented space. For vector-valued updates the corresponding identity holds with squared Euclidean norms. The weighted Poisson bound and a second-order drift estimate control its expectation along the adaptive path.

::: {#thm-augmented-ode-tracking}
## ODE tracking under Markov noise with contractive memory

Assume @prp-poisson-parameter and suppose that, uniformly for $\theta\in\mathsf K$,

$$
Q_\theta\mathcal V^2\leq a_2\mathcal V^2+b_2,
\qquad a_2<1,\quad b_2<\infty.
$$ {#eq-adaptive-quadratic-drift}

Let $\mathbb E[\mathcal V^2(Z_0)]<\infty$, and suppose the unprojected recursion @eq-augmented-controlled-sa remains in $\mathsf K$ almost surely. Assume also that $\sup_{\theta\in\mathsf K,z\in\mathsf Z}|G_\theta(z)|\leq B<\infty$. Let $(\gamma_n)$ be deterministic, positive and nonincreasing, with

$$
\gamma_n\to0,\qquad
\sum_n\gamma_n=\infty,\qquad
\sum_n\gamma_n^2(1+|\log\gamma_n|)<\infty.
$$ {#eq-log-gain-condition}

Then

$$
\sum_{n=0}^\infty\gamma_{n+1}
\bigl[G_{\theta_n}(Z_{n+1})-F(\theta_n)\bigr]
\quad\text{converges almost surely}.
$$ {#eq-centred-noise-summability}

If $F$ has a Lipschitz extension to a neighbourhood carrying its forward ODE flow, the piecewise-linear interpolation $\bar\theta$ on the timescale $t_n=\sum_{k=1}^n\gamma_k$ is an asymptotic pseudo-trajectory of $\dot\theta=F(\theta)$ (using that extension for the flow). In particular, for every $T>0$,

$$
\lim_{t\to\infty}\sup_{0\leq s\leq T}
|\bar\theta(t+s)-\Phi_s(\bar\theta(t))|=0
\qquad\text{almost surely}.
$$ {#eq-augmented-apt}
:::

::: {.proof}
Iterating @eq-adaptive-quadratic-drift conditionally shows $\sup_n\mathbb E[\mathcal V^2(Z_n)]<\infty$. The frozen Poisson and drift estimates give $|u_\theta|+|\phi_\theta|\leq C\mathcal V$. Using @eq-poisson-conditional-variance,

$$
\sum_n\gamma_{n+1}^2
\mathbb E[|\Delta M_{n+1}|^2]
\leq C\sum_n\gamma_{n+1}^2<\infty,
$$

so the weighted martingale converges almost surely.

For the remaining terms of @eq-controlled-poisson-decomposition, summation by parts yields, for $N\geq1$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\gamma_{n+1}
\bigl[G_{\theta_n}(Z_{n+1})-F(\theta_n)\bigr]\\
={}&\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\gamma_{n+1}\Delta M_{n+1}
+\gamma_1\phi_{\theta_0}(Z_0)
-\gamma_N\phi_{\theta_{N-1}}(Z_N)\\
&+\sum_{n=1}^{N-1}(\gamma_{n+1}-\gamma_n)\phi_{\theta_n}(Z_n)\\
&+\sum_{n=1}^{N-1}\gamma_n
\bigl[\phi_{\theta_n}(Z_n)-\phi_{\theta_{n-1}}(Z_n)\bigr].
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-adaptive-poisson-summation}

The terminal boundary term tends to zero almost surely, since its squared expectation is bounded by $C\gamma_N^2$ and $\sum_N\gamma_N^2<\infty$. The gain-variation series is absolutely summable almost surely because $\sum_n|\gamma_{n+1}-\gamma_n|<\infty$ and $\sup_n\mathbb E[\mathcal V(Z_n)]<\infty$.

Finally, $|\theta_n-\theta_{n-1}|\leq B\gamma_n$, and @eq-poisson-feedback-log-lipschitz gives, for all sufficiently large $n$,

$$
\gamma_n|\phi_{\theta_n}(Z_n)-\phi_{\theta_{n-1}}(Z_n)|
\leq C\gamma_n^2(1+|\log\gamma_n|)\mathcal V(Z_n).
$$ {#eq-adaptive-feedback-summable}

The right-hand side is summable almost surely by @eq-log-gain-condition and the uniform first-moment bound. Thus the weighted centred-noise series converges. The interpolated recursion is an Euler approximation of $F$ with vanishing accumulated noise on bounded time intervals; Lipschitz continuity of $F$ on $\mathsf K$ and the assumed flow extension give @eq-augmented-apt.
:::

For the bounded-innovation Adam representation in @eq-sqrt-memory-update, the readout meets the boundedness and Lipschitz assumptions above. The driver coupling, parameter regularity, quadratic moments and stability conditions are to be verified for the chosen adaptive MCMC kernel.
